headline: IonQ signed a DARPA agreement worth up to $300 million to have its quantum computers independently tested through 2029.
score_reason: Pool score 6 lowered by one: the announcement dates from 7 Oct and the final-round selection was already carried yesterday; the dollar value is the new fact. Company statement.
importance_line: The Pentagon's research agency will check whether IonQ's machines can reach useful scale, which matters to investors and government users watching for credible quantum hardware, but only the initial amount is committed and the full $300 million is potential.
summary: IonQ, a US quantum computing company, said on 7 Oct 2026 that it has reached Stage C, the final stage of DARPA's Quantum Benchmarking Initiative, under an agreement worth up to $300 million; yesterday Quantum Computing Report carried the news that IBM and three other makers had reached the same round. Only the initial amount is committed, the rest depends on future US funding decisions, and DARPA will test IonQ's Superion machines through 2029.
notes: Read the original IonQ release (the Fierce Network copy was blocked, HTTP 403). Announcement dated 7 Oct 2026; follows the 8 Oct item on the DARPA final-round selections.
